newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Bank Leumi offering approved.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Bank Leumi offering approved.

text.p: Israel's parliament finance committee has approved the sale of up to 20 percent of Bank Leumi to be floated in Tel Aviv, London, and perhaps other European cities before month's end, the Treasury said on Friday.
It said Thursday's committee approval, the last governmental hurdle to the offering, was unanimous.
A minimum of 10 percent of the shares must be sold. The government holds 82 percent of Leumi shares with the remainder already in the public domain.
Heads of Leumi and MI Holdings, the agency charged with selling state-owned banks, were expected return to Israel on Friday from a European roadshow aimed at wooing investors in the offering.

MI Holding Managing Director Meir Jacobsen said when the group left on May 4 that they expected to make an offering of 10 to 15 percent and that foreign institutional investors were expected to buy some 70 to 75 percent of that.
He said the government hoped to raise about $150 million from the sale.

Merrill Lynch and Lehman Brothers are the international distributors for the offering which will include shares and warrants. The government expects to raise three billion shekels from the sale of Israeli bank shares this year.
